note: Fork doc-payload classification (V2-506). Every file under docs/ (and the root HARNESS-V2-* program docs) is one of: 'fork' — a fork operating this template INHERITS it (ADRs, runbooks, recipes, rubrics, ledgers, the operational reference); or 'template-dev' — the TEMPLATE's own development history (the harness-v2/enterprise program artifacts, research, deep-comparison, verification evidence) that a fork does not need. `npm run rebrand -- --prune-docs` reads this to print the prune list. Prune semantics: on a FORK the template-dev docs are MOVED to an archive branch reference, NEVER deleted from template main. Rules are FIRST-MATCH-WINS, top to bottom; the final catch-all defaults to 'fork' so an unclassified doc is KEPT (the safe failure), and adding a new template-dev doc means adding an explicit rule above it.

rules.why: harness-v2 program artifacts (backlog/evidence/closeout) — the template's own build record
branch-only in-flight state; never reaches fork main

per-session in-flight state (the SESSION-HANDOFF.md data source) — never merged to main, pruned from forks (.claude/rules/harness.md Memory lifecycle). The schema (session-state.schema.json) stays fork-inherited: a fork regenerates its own state against it.
design-QA evidence for the template's own build (the pattern is inherited via the recipes/rubric, not the evidence)
feature blueprints for capabilities the fork inherits (openapi seam, docs-site, egress bridge, style-guide, asset-tracker pilot, README)
ADRs — the architectural decision record the fork operates under (incl. ADR-TEMPLATE)
operational + maintainer runbooks the fork inherits
seed parity matrices for the benchmark loop
catch-all: operational reference (REPO-MAP, recipes, rubrics, ledgers, agent-memory, oss-catalog, token-policy, mcp, session-state, manifests) — default KEEP is the safe failure
